stemBlocks.value: The formula converting degrees Celsius to degrees Fahrenheit is F = 9C/5 + 32. Make C the subject of the formula, then find the temperature in degrees Celsius when F = 95.
Think first: Rearrange first, substitute second - it is far safer than substituting into the un-rearranged formula.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p056-q15 from workbook page 56.

strategyBlocks.value: Subtract 32, multiply by 5 and divide by 9 to make C the subject, then put F = 95 into the result.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: C = 5(F - 32)/9, and when F = 95, C = 35 degrees Celsius

whyThisWorks.value: The 32 is added after the scaling, so it must be removed before the scaling is undone - that is why F - 32 appears as a whole bracket. Multiplying by 5/9 is the exact inverse of multiplying by 9/5, so the two formulae describe the same conversion read in opposite directions.

commonErrors.misconception: Dividing by 9 before subtracting 32, giving C = 5F/9 - 32.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Dividing by 9 before subtracting 32, giving C = 5F/9 - 32.

commonErrors.misconception: Multiplying by 9 and dividing by 5 instead of the other way round.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Multiplying by 9 and dividing by 5 instead of the other way round.

examTip.value: Rearrange the formula fully before you substitute any numbers - it keeps the algebra clean and earns method marks even if the arithmetic slips.
